text: This story is the treatment slice of legacy RWB-E2-018 and writes eight criteria of its own. The circuit and the eleven legacy criteria AC1 to AC11 stay with RWB-P6-E2018-APP, the signature request row with its five statuses and the signed copy stay with RWB-P5-E2018-APP and rwb-document, and the twelve legacy test case IDs are kept here with their Covers and Data unchanged.
why: The legacy key was one communications module and is split across rwb-comms, rwb-document and rwb-treatment, and the same eleven criteria cannot be owned twice; the work package carries the key as Split (rework) with an empty acs list for this story and marks it secondary, and the P6 and P5 slices publish the flow and the request.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 1 to 19, its section 7 acceptance criteria, section 12 published interfaces and section 16 test cases; TSD S2 T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and R7.2 s7; work package B2-S2-020 story line for RWB-S2-E2018-APP.
applied_in: Story sections 1, 7 (the reading after the criteria), 16 and 19; fragment acs and tcs
confirm: The owners of RWB-P6-E2018-APP and RWB-P5-E2018-APP confirm that the eleven legacy criteria and the signed copy are carried there.
impact: Low: no legacy criterion is restated or lost, and the flow and the request are proved in the other two slices.

text: The treatment side of the signature is carried on five nullable columns of its own treatment row - signature_method, signature_request_ref, signature_sent_at, signature_signed_at and signature_expires_at - beside DF-TRT-030 signature_status, with a unique index on the reference and an index on the status and the expiry, and on the additive properties of the two operations the service already declares; no fifth REST operation is added, because the ownership rows of S2 publish four and only four.
why: TSD S2 T3.1 gives the treatment signature_status and no other signature field, the legacy adds no treatment column, and creating a signature operation of its own would contradict the ownership rows the context pack fixes as the authority for service facts.
read: Context pack S2 ownership rows of S2 (four REST operations, one table, one event, one workflow); TSD S2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-030 and DF-TRT-010) and T-A.1 to T-A.2; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 11, 12 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13, DP-15 and R7.2 s12.
confirm: The rwb-treatment data owner approves the five columns and the two indexes in the DDL, and the owners of RWB-S2-E3001-CON and RWB-S2-E3002-CON accept the additive properties.
impact: Medium: if the update contract refuses the properties the record needs a sub-resource of its own, which is one operation entry and one C row on its caller and no change to a criterion.

text: The seam is read as a published REST contract with a mock: the signature record arrives on the update operation this service publishes on /api/recovery/treatment/v1, and the closure is announced on this service's own event. A later move to a Temporal activity on queue rwb-document, as the matrix cell has it, changes the client and no criterion.
why: DP-11 is in the pattern set and the legacy has a synchronous in-process interface across the seam, while Architecture v5 slide 13 gives S2 to P5 a Temporal cell and gives P6 and P5 no cell into S2, and no source publishes a signature activity on either of their queues for this capability, so the matrix alone leaves nothing to build against on Day 1.
read: Architecture v5 slides 8, 11 and 13 (row S2 Treatment: T to P5, nothing to P6; rows P6 Comms and P5 Document: nothing to S2); Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.5 DP-11 and R5.7; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 4 and 12; work package B2-S2-020 story line (DP-11 in the pattern set, all dependency lists empty); gap CG-B-P6-04-E2018-3 of the P6 slice.
confirm: The architecture review confirms the call type of the P6 and S2 seam before the contracts are frozen, with the rwb-comms and rwb-document owners.
impact: Medium: a move to Temporal rewrites the client and its fake and leaves every rule, value and criterion unchanged.

text: The method list LOV-SIGN-METHOD with E_SIGNATURE, BRANCH and PAPER and the status list LOV-TRT-SIGNATURE with PENDING, SIGNED and NOT_SIGNED are reference data read at their version through the reference-data contract of rwb-case, and the operation names of the two reads are taken from that contract; the signature basis, the conduct check and the provider vocabulary stay with rwb-comms and rwb-document and are not copied here.
why: The legacy records the method and request status lists as additions, no source names the operation of the reads as this service consumes them, and the treatment's own status column carries the three values TSD S2 T3.2 fixes, so leaving any of them as a constant would put a business value in code and a copy of another owner's vocabulary in this one.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07 and R7.2 s17; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 3, 8 (BR1) and 13; TSD S2 T3.2 (LOV-TRT-SIGNATURE) and T6.1; Architecture v5 slide 41 (templates with P6); context pack S2 DP table short form.
confirm: The P3 reference-data owner confirms the list codes and the operation names at the wave 2 contract freeze.
impact: Low: a renamed list or operation is a client change and a fixture change, and no criterion moves.

text: The reference-data client, the outbox and inbox library, the workflow kit and its durable timer, the per-service Flyway sequence and the gateway-bff composite route are platform wave-0 capability the service template already carries, so this story declares the nine patterns and the dependency each adds and keeps Depends on (build), Contract dependencies, Integration dependencies and External dependencies as the work package lists them, building against the fakes until the platform stories publish.
why: The pattern table adds five H rows and one C row for DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 while the work package's four dependency lists are empty; every added row is a platform library or a contract the template or another service publishes, and inventing a build row would change the plan's build sequence.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service from the service template and the shared libraries) and slide 8; work package B2-S2-020 story line for RWB-S2-E2018-APP.
applied_in: Story metadata, sections 3, 6, 12 and 13, and section 18 dependency rows
confirm: The platform template owner confirms the library and route delivery ahead of wave 2.
impact: Medium: a late library delays the build, but no H or C row is invented in the metadata.

text: The window is the treatment's own offer validity: the timer is the durable timer of the stage that RWB-S2-E3007-APP starts at send, this story supplies the closure callback it invokes, and the closure writes NOT_SIGNED with reason OFFER_EXPIRED and announces it once. The outcome rather than the intent is what the parent CaseWorkflow hears, and it moves the case under R-RES-16, R-RES-17, R-RES-18, R-SET-10, R-SET-11 or R-DIL-18. No case status, task or timer is read or written by this service.
why: The legacy has P3 announce OFFER_EXPIRED and call the signature module from the case side, while Architecture v5 gives the treatment its offer validity and gives rwb-case the case status, and DP-10 replaces the Quartz job with a Temporal timer; the two readings must be reconciled before a criterion can name who closes the window.
read: Context pack S2 (one workflow TreatmentWorkflow, no job of S2) and the Temporal and Drools slides (S2: the 14-day offer and the plan timers); Architecture v5 slides 3, 11 and 18; TSD S2 T4 (R-RES-16 to R-RES-18, R-SET-10, R-SET-11); legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 4 (step 9), 8 (BR5) and 9; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10 and DP-12.
confirm: The owner of RWB-S2-E3007-APP and the rwb-case owner of the case workflow confirm the split at the wave 2 build start.
impact: Medium: if the case must close the window, one inbound call is added and the timer stays where it is, and the criteria of AC4 keep their values.

text: The party rows of the case are read from the service's own read-only v_ace_customer view, SELECT only, to check that the party a record names belongs to the case; no name, national identifier, address or signature image is read or stored, and the basis check, the conduct check, the EasyApp leg and the signed version are rwb-comms' and rwb-document's. If the platform keeps the ACE views to rwb-source-data, the read moves to that contract and a C row appears.
why: DP-05 allows either the contract of rwb-source-data or the service's own views, the work package lists no C dependency, the legacy data table names v_ace_customer person_key as a read, and the guardrails forbid personal data in events, workflow inputs and logs.
read: Context pack S2 (ACE data only through the owner's contract or v_ace_* views; DP-05); legacy RWB-E2-018 section 11 (DF-ACE-056 person_key) and section 17; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17; NFR-052 and CTL-11.
confirm: The rwb-source-data owner with the rwb-treatment tech lead at the wave 2 build start.
impact: Low: the payload is narrower than the sources allow, and a move to the contract adds one C row and one client.

text: No personal data is written, logged or published by this story: the row, the two events, the log lines and the workflow input carry the case ID, the treatment ID, the party KEY, the method code, the status code, the provider reference and the times only, the profile codec is on every payload, and a property test fails the build if a name, a national identifier, a signature image or a PDF byte reaches a column, a log line or a span attribute.
why: Template and Rules section R7.2 s17 and the legacy guardrails forbid personal data in events, workflow inputs and logs, and the signed document must stay write-once in its owner's custody (CTL-12, NFR-052).
read: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17; legacy RWB-E2-018 sections 11 and 17; CTL-11, CTL-12 and NFR-052; Architecture v5 slide 22 notes.
confirm: The privacy owner confirms the field set of the treatment read and of the two events.
impact: Low: the payload is narrower than the sources allow and the signed document never leaves its owner.

text: The signature state reaches SCR-14 Treatment record through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the treatment read of this service with the document read of rwb-document and the request list of rwb-comms, one hop each and read only; SCR-30 shows the signed version from the document read and SCR-09 lists the comms exception entries, and the route path, the screen field list, the merge order and the layout belong to the edge contract and the screen owners.
why: DP-19 replaces the monolith screen with a composite route and no source publishes the route or the field list of these three screens in this wave, while the browser may call no owner service directly.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19 and R7.2 s15; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 20 (gateway-bff, one hop, 2 s, breaker per service); legacy RWB-E2-018 section 15.
confirm: The owner of RWB-PLT-N001-CON publishes the SCR-14 route and its merge order with the screen owners.
impact: Low: the read model is proved against the route fake and switched on with the screens.
